records.title: Introducing advanced tool use on the Claude Developer Platform
records.relevance_note: Deferred tool loading cuts token load and preserves cacheable prefixes.
records.reason_included: Concrete mechanism for tool-surface cost control in agent loops.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Loading only a search tool plus 3-5 relevant tools reduced upfront context from about 77K tokens to about 8.7K tokens, preserving 95% of the context window.
Deferred tools marked with `defer_loading: true` are excluded from the initial prompt and expanded into context only after search-time selection.
Because deferred tools are excluded from the initial prompt, the system prompt and core tool definitions remain cacheable.
The feature adds a search step before invocation, so the context savings and accuracy gains trade off against added latency.

records.title: Shell](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/advanced-tool-use%22},{%22source_id%22:%22src_doc_126c6de9bbb9%22,%22title%22:%22Shell) + Skills + Compaction: Tips for long-running agents that do real work
records.relevance_note: Long-run agent guidance ties cost control to thread reuse and compaction.
records.reason_included: Direct long-horizon cost and continuity patterns from provider engineering.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Hosted shell requests carry stateful work, tool calls, multi-turn continuation, and artifacts through the Responses API.
Server-side compaction runs automatically in-stream once context crosses a threshold, avoiding a separate compaction call.
For long runs, OpenAI recommends reusing the same container, passing `previous_response_id`, and using compaction as a default primitive rather than an emergency fallback.
Moving templates and examples into skills avoids inflating tokens for unrelated queries because they load only when the skill triggers.

records.title: Prompt](https://developers.openai.com/blog/skills-shell-tips%22},{%22source_id%22:%22src_doc_6cefd45b6af9%22,%22title%22:%22Prompt) Caching 201
records.relevance_note: OpenAI cookbook gives concrete cache-hit rules, telemetry fields, and cache-preserving prompt layout.
records.reason_included: Implementation-level caching mechanics plus cost/accounting guidance.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Cache hits require an exact repeated prefix, start at 1024 tokens, and accrue in 128-token increments; the cacheable prefix includes messages, images, audio, tool definitions, and structured output schemas.
In-memory prompt caching works automatically, extended caching can last up to 24 hours, and `prompt_cache_key` can improve routing for traffic that shares prefixes.
Responses expose per-request cache telemetry through `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`, enabling direct measurement of cached versus uncached prompt tokens.
At around 150k+ tokens, cached requests were reported as 67% faster on time-to-first-token, and a slightly longer but stable prefix can be cheaper than a shorter prompt that never caches.

Changing tool definitions, schemas, ordering, or early dynamic values invalidates exact-prefix matching; the guide recommends keeping stable tools ordered identically and moving volatile metadata out of the prompt prefix.

records.title: Prompt](https://developers.openai.com/cookbook/examples/prompt_caching_201%22},{%22source_id%22:%22src_doc_ac681845490f%22,%22title%22:%22Prompt) caching - Claude API Docs
records.relevance_note: Detailed invalidation, TTL, and usage-field behavior for Anthropic prompt caching.
records.reason_included: Strong provider doc with cache-consistency and failure-mode detail.

claim_snippets.claim_text: By default the cache lifetime is 5 minutes and refreshes with use; Anthropic also offers a 1-hour cache duration at additional cost.
Automatic prefix checking uses one breakpoint at the end of static content and reuses the longest previously written prefix.
When thinking blocks are read from cache they still count as input tokens in usage metrics, which matters for cost calculation and token budgeting.
Tool-result-only user messages keep cache validity, but adding non-tool-result user content invalidates prior thinking blocks and starts a new assistant loop.
Length-based caching failures are silent and cache keys can also break from changing `tool_choice`, image presence, or unstable JSON key ordering in `tool_use` blocks.

records.title: [Bug](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching%22},{%22source_id%22:%22src_iss_c1f147f856cb%22,%22title%22:%22[Bug)]: Prompt cache constantly invalidated — cacheWrite dominates over cacheRead, causing 10x cost increase
records.relevance_note: Regression report with per-call cost evidence and cache read/write imbalance.
records.reason_included: Concrete real-world cache failure with operational cost impact.

claim_snippets.claim_text: After upgrading to 2026.2.17, a ~20k-token system prompt was reportedly rewritten to cache on nearly every call, increasing cost from roughly $0.02-$0.04 to $0.35-$0.50 per call.
The reporter compares pre-upgrade sessions where `cacheRead` dominated after the first call with post-upgrade sessions where `cacheWrite` dominated and cost rose to as high as $0.51.
Several recent calls incurred about $0.50 with zero output, suggesting the full context was being sent and cache-written without producing useful work.
The issue ties diagnosis to session JSONL usage entries that expose `cacheWrite >> cacheRead`, making cache-read/write ratios a practical regression detector.

claim_locations.locator: Issue description and cost comparison, lines 206-219
Examples of high-cost zero-output calls, lines 224-230

records.title: Agent](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/19989%22},{%22source_id%22:%22src_iss_985d6091dfd3%22,%22title%22:%22Agent) SDK defaults to 1-hour cache TTL instead of 5-minute
records.relevance_note: Shows how TTL defaults surface in usage fields and directly change cost.
records.reason_included: Useful failure case for cache TTL governance and cost attribution.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The reporter states the Agent SDK shifted cache creation from 5-minute TTL to 1-hour TTL by default, with all cache-creation tokens landing in `ephemeral_1h_input_tokens` and none in `ephemeral_5m_input_tokens`.
The issue reports a direct pricing consequence: 1-hour cache writes are billed at 2x base input price versus 1.25x for 5-minute writes.

The reproduction output includes `total_cost_usd`, `cache_creation_input_tokens`, `cache_read_input_tokens`, and a nested `cache_creation` object, making per-run attribution visible in returned usage.

claim_locations.locator: Issue summary and usage fields, lines 205-209, 255-258, 286
Reproduction output showing attribution fields, lines 233-258

records.title: High](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-typescript/issues/188%22},{%22source_id%22:%22src_iss_3dddd3e1acbc%22,%22title%22:%22High) token usage due to Prompt Cache in agents (large cached fixed context) – bug or expected behavior?
records.relevance_note: User report isolates agent-specific fixed-context cost blowup on trivial queries.
records.reason_included: Good example of silent fixed-prefix cost in agent wrappers.

claim_snippets.claim_text: For simple queries, the reporter observed very low `promptTokens.input` but very high `promptTokens.write` at 20k-30k tokens and `promptTokens.read` at 0, implying a large fixed cached context rather than user input dominated cost.
The issue happened with agents but not simple chat sessions, suggesting the prompt assembly path for agents injected substantial static overhead.
Changing models reduced cache size materially, indicating model-specific prompt assembly or wrapper differences can change fixed-context cost.
The thread explicitly identifies unclear controls for cache invalidation, excluding certain blocks from caching, or disabling prompt caching per agent.

records.title: [Bug](https://github.com/danny-avila/LibreChat/discussions/11615%22},{%22source_id%22:%22src_iss_2b9f1f0c5a91%22,%22title%22:%22[Bug)]: Prompt-cache not used because OpenClaw is changing the prompt-prefix (inference costs x1000)
records.relevance_note: Shows prompt-prefix drift causing repeated recomputation in long multi-turn runs.
records.reason_included: Clear cache-consistency failure with server-log clues.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The reporter attributes prompt-cache failure to the application changing the prompt prefix, forcing recomputation on each message and creating very high inference cost.
The issue reports about 40k additional computed tokens per message on top of an initial 40k context, with the multiplier becoming severe over long workflows.
Only the first ~70k tokens reportedly used the existing prompt cache; after that the rest was recomputed and llama-server logged invalidated context checkpoints.

records.title: Prompt caching - Claude API Docs
records.relevance_note: Definitive provider documentation detailing block-level prompt caching syntax, cost multipliers, and TTL extension mechanisms crucial for long-horizon agent stability.
records.reason_included: Mandatory coverage of explicit block-level caching semantics and the precise economic tradeoffs between 5-minute and 1-hour cache lifespans.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Anthropic allows developers to define up to four distinct cache_control breakpoints... enforcing a strict hierarchical evaluation order: tools, then system instructions, then messages.
A 1-hour cache write incurs a 2.0x base input price multiplier, compared to the 1.25x multiplier applied to 5-minute writes.
Changes to tool_choice or the presence/absence of images anywhere in the prompt will invalidate the cache, requiring a new cache entry to be created.

claim_snippets.claim_text: CTA-PROMPTED achieved a 94.0% optimal policy match rate by allowing the agent to dynamically shift its retrieval threshold based on varying costs.
CTA-RL improved discounted reward by 3.5% in a coding task... demonstrating more adaptive and cost-efficient decision-making compared to baseline end-to-end RL.

records.title: qhkm/zeptoclaw: Final form of claw family
records.relevance_note: A prime architectural example of shifting context compaction out of the provider SDK and into modular middleware stacks to protect analytical workspaces.
records.reason_included: Demonstrates strict non-LLM-dependent execution bounds, deterministic loop guards, and stratified memory structures in a production codebase.

claim_snippets.claim_text: ZeptoClaw implements per-session budget enforcement and per-model cost estimation for 8 models at the gateway layer.
Constructs middleware stacks including CompactionMiddleware and TokenBudgetMiddleware to intercept the context array before network calls.

records.title: Automatic context compaction
records.relevance_note: Explains Anthropic's native compaction architecture via the SDK, which substitutes detailed historical context with synthesized XML summaries.
records.reason_included: Meets requirement for an engineering writeup on context compaction, showcasing both its utility in continuous operation and its tradeoff with precise historical data preservation.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The compaction_control parameter... intercepts the loop when token usage exceeds a threshold, injects a summary prompt, and replaces the history with a generated <summary>.
While compaction manages token budgets... early-stage data gathering feeding into late-stage synthesis is inadvertently destroyed, resulting in a 'summary of summaries'.

records.title: DeepSeek API introduces Context Caching on Disk, cutting prices by an order of magnitude
records.exception_reason: Pioneering architectural implementation of Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA) disk-backed caching that permanently altered baseline economics for agentic systems.
records.relevance_note: Describes DeepSeek's shift from expensive VRAM KV caching to disk-backed structures, enabling highly aggressive caching logic.
records.reason_included: Critical technical background on how model providers implement sub-100-token increment caching and its radical effect on agent operational budgets.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The MLA architecture compresses the context KV cache, enabling offloading to low-cost distributed disk arrays, reducing costs to $0.014 per million tokens for cache hits.
Evaluates prompt prefixes in minute increments of just 64 tokens, circumventing the 1,024-token minimums enforced by other providers.
